title: Septic Service Preventive Maintenance Checklist Form
subtitle: Control site assessment, safe access, inspection, pumping, maintenance, transport, and handoff through verified identity, domain-specific observations, evidence, authorization, exception ownership, and accountable closeout.
description: An original, workflow-complete septic service preventive maintenance checklist for tanks, baffles, pumps, controls, distribution components, and drainfield observations. It connects system records, approved scope, and disposal authority to present conditions, repeatable evidence, decisions, unresolved work, and the receiving party's handoff.
use_case: Use when a qualified septic-service technician must perform scheduled septic service maintenance against an identified plan while preserving readings, defects, deferrals, verification, and the next due event.

sections.title: Septic Service preventive service tasks and controlled materials
sections.guidance: Separate tasks completed from tasks merely considered, and preserve product, part, quantity, and removed-item custody.

blocks.label: Preventive maintenance tasks completed
items: Locate and secure system access
Open and inspect accessible components without entry
Measure sludge, scum, liquid level, and accessible condition
Pump the authorized tank or compartment
Clean approved filter or serviceable component
Inspect baffles, tees, risers, lids, pumps, floats, and alarms
Record repairs completed and additional work recommended
Secure load and complete transport manifest
Deliver septage to the approved receiving facility
Restore covers, grade, controls, and customer access

sections.title: Septic Service measurements and post-maintenance verification
sections.guidance: Use repeatable observations to show the maintained scope reached the stated condition.

blocks.label: Measurement and verification log
blocks.guidance: Applicable measurement concepts include: Tank or compartment capacity, Sludge depth or distance to outlet, Scum depth or clearance, Liquid level or operating condition, Pumped volume or load quantity, Pump, float, alarm, flow, or electrical reading.

blocks.label: Post-maintenance condition and function checks
items: Authorized tank or compartment was inspected and serviced
Pumped volume and remaining condition are documented
Baffles, tees, filter, pump, float, and alarm status are recorded
No visible spill, open access, unsecured cover, or uncontrolled exposure remains
Vehicle, manifest, receiving facility, and disposal receipt reconcile
System power, alarms, covers, grade, and access are restored
Failure indicators and repair recommendations have an owner and due point
Customer received use, water, maintenance, and emergency guidance

blocks.label: Maintenance evidence retained

Sludge, scum, liquid-level, and capacity measurements
Drainfield and site-condition observations
Pumped compartment and volume record
Vehicle, operator, manifest, and load reference
Approved receiving-facility receipt
Restoration, repair recommendation, and customer instruction record

sections.title: Septic Service defect containment and corrective-action routing
sections.guidance: A preventive checklist does not release an unsafe, unverified, or out-of-scope condition.

blocks.label: Septic Service exception and stop-work indicators
items: Tank location, access, buried utility, or component identity uncertain
Cover, riser, tank, soil, or surrounding surface appears unstable
Confined-space entry, fall-in, engulfment, toxic gas, or oxygen concern
Ignition source, fire, explosion, electrical, or mechanical exposure
Sewage contact, splash, aerosol, spill, backup, or public exposure
Hose, vacuum, valve, truck, cap, containment, or traffic control defective
Unexpected industrial, hazardous, chemical, or prohibited waste suspected
Pumping may damage an unknown, fragile, or structurally compromised component
Transport manifest, vehicle authorization, facility acceptance, or disposal route unavailable
System failure, surfacing effluent, contamination, or repair need exceeds scope
blocks.guidance: Select the observed condition; do not use a generic exception when the actual trigger is known.

sections.title: Septic Service preventive maintenance checklist closeout and accountable handoff
sections.guidance: Close only when outcome, remaining limitation, next action, evidence, and receiving ownership agree.

blocks.label: Final outcome, handoff, and record location
Record boundary and stop condition
blocks.guidance: This septic service preventive maintenance checklist is an operational record, not a substitute for applicable law, licensing, product labeling, manufacturer instructions, site policy, safety requirements, or professional judgment. Stop affected work, access, application, operation, testing, or release when tank access, collapse, confined-space, toxic or flammable atmosphere, sewage exposure, buried utility, pumping, transport, disposal, or system condition is uncertain. A septic, wastewater, or safety supervisor must review the exception, authorize the controlling decision, and preserve its evidence before closeout.
